## What I did

**1. Started the stack with the existing script, unchanged**

Ran `node start-stack.mjs` from the project root. I did not modify, split, or rewrite it — the script itself performs the full sequence (`start-backend` → `verify-backend` → `start-frontend` → `verify-frontend`) and exits nonzero on any failure. Output:

```

OK {"role":"backend","instance":"e13d2c7e-...","url":"http://127.0.0.1:10441",...}
OK {"status":"started","role":"frontend","instance":"fd86beee-...","url":"http://127.0.0.1:10448","pid":42836,"project":"developer-demo","version":"2.0.0"}
OK {"role":"frontend","instance":"fd86beee-...","url":"http://127.0.0.1:10448",...}
```

**2. Independently verified both services are ready**

I re-checked with the project's own verifiers rather than trusting the script's exit code:

| Service | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Backend | `node dev.mjs verify-backend` | exit 0 — healthy, instance `e13d2c7e-…`, port 10441, pid 25292 |
| Frontend | `node dev.mjs verify-frontend` | exit 0 — healthy, instance `fd86beee-…`, port 10448, pid 42836 |
